findings.sequence_description: I1 issuer binding: compare default IdP config (no pinned issuer) vs pinned issuer config; attempt login with wrong Issuer to detect whether verification policy is applied to consumed Issuer semantics.

Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_wrong_issuer_default_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_wrong_issuer_default_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Default-config SAML IdP accepted assertion with arbitrary/untrusted Issuer (issuer validation skipped or misapplied).

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after forcing a user-wide logout. Replay caches must not be cleared by session logout; second acceptance indicates replay protection scoped incorrectly to session state.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_replay_attacker_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_replay_attacker_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted a replayed SAML assertion ID after user logout; replay cache appears incorrectly scoped to session state.

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: verify baseline SAML login works, then submit an expired assertion (NotOnOrAfter 60 minutes in the past). Also perform a second valid login as a different identity to ensure multi-identity coverage and rule out global broker failure.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); expiry/freshness checks are not enforced.

findings.sequence_description: Attempt to bypass SAML assertion replay detection by replaying the same Assertion/@ID across two different SAML IdP aliases within the same realm (tests whether replay cache is incorrectly scoped only per-provider alias). Includes two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_replay_b_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_replay_b_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML Assertion/@ID via a different IdP alias (replay cache scoped incorrectly)

findings.sequence_description: Replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after modifying the SAME IdP instance configuration (PUT) to test whether replay cache is incorrectly cleared/invalidated by config updates. Includes two identities and a config change + re-auth.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_after_change_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_after_change_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML Assertion/@ID after IdP config change (replay cache cleared by config update)

findings.sequence_description: Test whether SAML assertion replay protection is incorrectly tied to realm/session token TTL settings: perform a successful SAML login, then change realm access token lifespan, then replay the exact same Assertion/@ID. Second acceptance would indicate replay cache invalidation or missing anti-replay enforcement after TTL-related config changes.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML assertion ID after realm TTL change (replay cache missing or incorrectly invalidated)

findings.sequence_description: I3: Initiate OIDC auth (SP-initiated) then attempt to complete SAML login against a different provider alias than the one intended, simulating RelayState/InResponseTo swap across providers within the same realm.

Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_wrongprov_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_wrongprov_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML completion on a different provider alias than the initiating flow; indicates cross-provider flow splicing (RelayState/InResponseTo not bound to provider).

findings.sequence_description: I5: Attempt SAML login with missing Conditions (no audience/time bounds). Then harden broker config and re-attempt. Uses two identities (control + attacker) and a config change with re-auth.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Even after broker configuration changes, Keycloak must not grant authorization when SAML assertion omits Conditions (no audience/time bounds). If accepted, effective permissions can exceed upstream intent and broker policy.

sequences.description: I5 attack: attempt SAML login with Conditions present but without AudienceRestriction (remove_conditions=false). Hypothesis: broker fails to enforce audience scoping and still mints an OIDC session that can be used to obtain authorization decisions for a protected resource (over-grant beyond upstream intent). Uses control password identity + attacker SAML identity (>=2 identities).
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: If Keycloak accepts a brokered SAML assertion that lacks AudienceRestriction (or otherwise does not bind the assertion to the intended SP/client), it may mint an OIDC session whose effective permissions exceed the upstream intent (audience-scoped authentication) intersected with broker policy.
